All requirements are implemented and verified. Let me update the handoff notes and do a final full run.

{"action":"shell","command":"cd /testbed && printf '%s\\n' '# tinydb milestone 1 + 2 - HANDOFF' '' 'Implemented tinydb/journal.py with BatchWriter(db) (default table only).' '' 'R01: apply(ops) validates list of op dicts; insert/remove; returns inserted ids; empty->[]; malformed->ValueError.' 'R02: atomic - deep-copied storage snapshot before batch; on any error restore default table + reset table._next_id + clear_cache; missing remove id is an error; previously acquired handles reflect success and rollback.' 'R03: ordinary API intact; deep-copy on insert (no aliasing either direction).' 'R04: bool doc_id rejected (isinstance bool check before int); structural validation of the whole batch before committing (non-list ops, non-dict ops, unknown op, missing keys, non-dict document -> ValueError); empty dict documents accepted.' 'R05: preview(ops) simulates on a deep copy of table data; never writes, never consumes IDs, never touches query cache; next ID mirrors Table._get_next_id (handle _next_id counter if set, else max(id)+1); errors (missing remove) raise ValueError after consuming nothing.' 'R05b: preview/apply return fresh detached lists; mutating them has no effect.' 'R05 (round 2): successful apply advances the table next-insertion-ID state and persists it via the storage (_update_table writes the table; _get_next_id caches the counter on the handle); subsequent inserts via apply or direct db.insert continue the sequence without reuse/rewind, even across removes. Failed apply restores _next_id (no IDs consumed).' 'R06: no cached initial snapshot - every apply/preview re-reads storage, so direct db.insert between calls is seen.' '' 'Conflict resolution (packet): the older note claiming preview may consume IDs and bool IDs are accepted is UNVERIFIED and SUPERSEDED by R04/R05 - implemented per current requirements (preview consumes nothing; bool rejected). Recorded in BatchWriter docstring.' '' 'Tests: tests/test_journal.py (123 tests, memory + JSON storage). Full tests/ + acceptance_public.py = 350 passed.' 'Notes: use where(...) for queries; run pytest with -o addopts= (pytest.ini has cov flags); storage may store IDs as strings (JSON) - preview normalises via int(); preview must not mutate table._next_id (it would consume an ID).'" > HANDOFF.md && python -m pytest tests/ acceptance_public.py -q -o addopts= 2>&1 | tail -3"}
